newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher on cash, short covering.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher on cash, short covering.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended broadly higher led by nearby December, which surged late on the buoyant cash market and on technical short-covering, traders said.
"The cash basis was on fire, a KCBT trader said. "Once we breached $4.12 and $4.14 in the December contract, that forced in additional short covering and technical-type buying."

Cash basis bids for hard red winter wheat in Kansas City jumped eight cents per bushel during Friday's session because of a lack of producer selling and continued strong domestic flour mill demand, traders said.
They also noted that KCBT wheat was supported by ongoing concerns over rain delays in Argentina's wheat harvest and by concerns about the milling quality of the European crop.
Wheat also drew strength from news that Turkey eased its ergot limit for wheat, barley and rye imports to 0.05 percent from 0.02 percent.
KCBT wheat closed one to nine cents per bushel higher, with December up nine cents at $4.16. The Dec/March spread widened to trade at 29 cents late after opening at around 24 cents.

Rosenthal Collins and Cargill Investor Services were each late buyers of Dec. RC bought one million Dec on the day and CIS picked up 1.6 million Dec. Man International bought 1.3 million Dec bushels. LFG sold one million each of Dec and March.
Prudential Securities bear-spread 1.8 million March/Dec bushels at between 24-1/2 and 28-1/2 cents. FIMAT was active on both sides of the spread, traders said.
